title: Quantinuum Details Nexus Hybrid Workflow Runtime Integration with Slurm and OpenQSE at SC26 - Quantum Computing Report
gist: At SC26, Quantinuum showed its Nexus Hybrid Workflow Runtime (Tierkreis) plugging Guppy quantum programs into HPC schedulers (Slurm, PBS, PJSub) within ORNL's OpenQSE architecture, using NVIDIA's Slurm 26.11 quantum extensions. A joint RIKEN chemistry workflow on a 12-atom hydrogen chain found quantum-sampled configurations reached lower ground-state energies than classical-only selection.

insights.claim: Quantinuum's Nexus platform includes an asynchronous Hybrid Workflow Runtime (Tierkreis) designed to coordinate multi-stage quantum-classical pipelines without leaving classical HPC nodes idle while remote quantum jobs wait in queues.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Idle-node cost is a key friction for quantum-HPC adoption; software that removes it strengthens Quantinuum's position as an HPC-integrated vendor beyond hardware.
insights.quote: without idling classical nodes while remote quantum jobs wait in queues

insights.claim: Quantinuum's Tierkreis runtime links its Guppy quantum programming language with existing HPC workload schedulers including Slurm, PBS, and PJSub, so quantum jobs plug into established supercomputer job management rather than requiring new infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Support for PJSub (used on Japanese systems like those at RIKEN) alongside Slurm/PBS signals Quantinuum targeting national-lab HPC centers globally.

insights.claim: In the Oak Ridge National Laboratory-led Open Quantum-HPC Software Ecosystem (OpenQSE) reference architecture, Quantinuum's Hybrid Workflow Runtime sits at the application workflow layer, above cluster scheduling and resource-access interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A layered, standardized quantum-HPC stack is forming; vendors that occupy the workflow/orchestration layer may capture developer lock-in independent of which QPU runs the job.
insights.quote: operates at the application workflow layer above cluster scheduling and resource-access interfaces
insights.locator: Within the Open Quantum-HPC Software Ecosystem

insights.claim: In Quantinuum's SC26 demo, the runtime dispatched classical chemistry steps to a shared Slurm executor using NVIDIA's Slurm 26.11 quantum resource extensions while routing quantum execution targets through QFw.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: NVIDIA's Slurm 26.11 QPU scheduling is becoming a common integration point; NVIDIA is positioning itself as the classical control plane of hybrid quantum computing regardless of QPU vendor.
insights.quote: alongside NVIDIA’s Slurm 26.11 quantum resource extensions

insights.claim: Quantinuum and RIKEN ran a joint electronic-structure workflow implementing RIKEN's quantum residual exploration method, using Guppy to define circuits and Tierkreis to manage classical-quantum handoffs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows Quantinuum's software stack being used in real national-lab science collaborations, a proof point for hybrid quantum chemistry use cases.

insights.claim: On a stretched 12-atom hydrogen chain, quantum-sampled electronic configuration proposals achieved lower calculated ground-state energies than classical-only selection using an identical number of final configurations, per Quantinuum and RIKEN.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An early, small-scale signal of quantum-assisted advantage in configuration selection for chemistry; watch whether it scales to larger, classically hard molecules before treating it as commercial advantage.
insights.quote: achieved lower calculated ground-state energies than classical-only selection using an identical number of final configurations
